Resolves #18865

Related: #18762

🪢 *Two questions D#17832 left open about an edit whose cell scrolls out of the DOM: can an editor refuse to be suspended, and does text being composed by an IME get lost? Now a column can opt out — and no, it does not.*

## The IME probe, and what it means for S4

Measured in Chromium through CDP (`Input.imeSetComposition`) on the pooled fixture: start a composition in an open editor, scroll the row out of the pool mid-composition, scroll back.

- Every composing `input` (`isComposing: true`) reaches the App Worker, so the draft already holds the composed text — `にほ` — when the node goes.
- No `compositionend` ever fires for the removed node, and none is needed.
- The reprojected editor shows the text, and Enter commits it.

What is lost is the IME's conversion state — the candidate window for the characters already entered — never text. **S4, blocking the pool while a composition is in flight, is not needed for data integrity**; it would only buy conversion convenience, at the price of the fixed-pool invariant. No S4 leaf is filed. The arm `a composition in flight when the row leaves the pool survives as the draft` pins the behaviour. Limits: one engine (Chromium), a synthetic composition; a platform IME could differ in events, not in what the App Worker has already received.

## The S3 opt-out

- `grid.column.Base#cancelEditOnProjectionLoss` (default `false`): for an editor holding state only its DOM has.
- `grid.Body#createViewData` reports every finished render pass to the editing plugin — the one place an embodiment can go, whatever caused it (scroll, sort, filter, the column window).
- `grid.plugin.CellEditing#onBodyRender` cancels the session of an opted-out column once its embodiment is lost, with `reason: 'projectionLoss'`. The default stays suspend-and-reproject.
- **No cancel is silent** (review round 1): `cancelEdit(reason)` fires `cellEditCancel {dataField, reason, record}` itself, once the session is over — `escape`, `notEditable`, `disabled`, `destroy` (the plugin went, its grid lives on), `projectionLoss`, or `api` for a caller that names none. A grid destroyed with its plugin never reaches `cancelEdit` and fires nothing.
- Only an embodiment that existed can be lost (`session.wasEmbodied`): a session born suspended by a Tab, on its way into sight, is left alone.
- A lock change (#18897) holds the editor out of every cell while the bodies swap columns, and re-embeds a new node. For an opted-out column that is a loss like any other: the bodies' render pass cancels and announces it, the release embeds nothing, and the next edit opens. Default columns never enter the branch.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real keys and CDP composition, CI-executed e2e tier) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: capability (`feat`).

## Deltas from ticket

- **Review round 1 (@neo-opus-ada): the event now means what its name says.** It fired on one of five cancel paths while its name and `reason` field promised all of them; changing that after a merge breaks someone either way. Moving the fire into `cancelEdit(reason)` also made `onBodyRender` smaller. The ticket asked only for the projection-loss announcement.
- **Rebased onto #18897, which merged first.** Two textual conflicts (the `session` docblock and `startEdit`'s `setSession` literal; the driver's action list), no design clash. The composed case got its own arm and its own mutation (P6).
- **No new engine event.** The obvious hook, an `unmounted` event on `component.Base`, would have fired for every component's unmount to serve one plugin. The Body already has the single place where an embodiment can go; it reports the pass, as `grid.Container` already reports `onColumnEditableChange` to the same plugin.
- **`wasEmbodied` looked untestable, and was not.** With the guard removed every arm stayed green — until the opted-out column was a LOCKED one: the bodies render one after another, so while the center body reports its pass, a born-suspended edit on `c39` has not been rendered by the end body yet, and was cancelled before it was ever shown. That is the arm on `c38 → c39`.
- The fixture's pooled grid gains one opted-out column, `c7`, and writes the `cellEditCancel` it receives onto its own node as a class, so a Brain-free spec can read the event. The locked-column arm opts `c39` out itself, at runtime, through the fixture's worker-side driver (`optOutEnd`).
- **The first head broke a neighbour, and the second commit is the repair.** It opted `c39` out in the fixture itself, and `CellEditingLockedBodies.spec.mjs` edits that column to witness S2 in the locked-end body — `e2e-engine` went red on that arm. A fixture column another witness reads keeps its default. My local neighbour run had shown it: I read only the summary's last line, `55 passed`, above which stood `1 failed`.

## Test Evidence

Re-run on the rebased head (base `dev@98dd1d7d76`, with #18897 under it) — pooling + suspended-Tab + locked-bodies specs, 23 arms:

| Mutation | Red arms |
|---|---|
| P1 the opt-out config is ignored | both cannot-suspend arms (row leaves the pool · lock change) |
| P2 `grid.Body` never reports its render pass | both cannot-suspend arms |
| P3 a session that was never embodied counts as lost | born suspended on a locked column (5 of 5) |
| P4 the cancel is not announced | both cannot-suspend arms |
| P5 every column cancels on projection loss | twelve S2 arms across the three specs: horizontal · vertical · the composition · born suspended · three suspended-Tab arms · five locked-bodies arms |
| C1 a cancel announces nothing | six arms: Escape · disabled · not editable · plugin destroyed (component) · both cannot-suspend arms (e2e) |
| C2 every cancel claims the default reason | the same six |
| C3 a commit announces a cancel too | the component Enter arm · born suspended on a locked column |
| P6 a held session still counts as embodied (#18897's clause in `isEmbodied`) | cannot-suspend under a lock change — the only arm that pins the clause |

C3 first came back with the Enter arm GREEN: a class the App Worker writes lands a render after the gesture, so "not there yet" passed. The arm now waits for a later cancel through the same channel before it reads the absence.

Neighbours, each run read for a `failed` line and none found: e2e `grid` 58, component `grid` 39, unit `grid` 132 passed; the five cancel-path component arms `--repeat-each=20` → 100 passed. Stability: the four new arms `--repeat-each=20` → 80 passed; before the rebase, the locked-end S2 arm the first head broke ran 20× green beside them. One flake found and fixed on the way: a double-click right after a horizontal scroll hit a cell the App Worker was still re-slotting (4 of 5 red); the arm now waits for `isScrolling` to end, as its sibling does.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge:** `cellEditCancel {dataField, record, reason}` is the grid's first edit-lifecycle event. Its name and its `reason` field read as "an edit was cancelled, and here is why", but only `onBodyRender` fires it. Escape, a column turning non-editable, `disabled`, and a plugin destroyed on its own all cancel silently. A consumer who listens for it to discard external state on cancel will miss the commonest cancel, Escape. That is the Required Action below.
- **Documented search:** I looked for other render paths that can take the editor out without `createViewData`. A record update repaints the same cell, and the plugin's own `repaint()` and #18897's hold go through `repaintRow()`, where a hold is followed by the bodies' passes anyway. I found no gap in "the one place an embodiment can go". I also checked the interplay with #18897: a cancel while held nulls the session, so `releaseEdit()` and the owed blur both find nothing, as they should.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass. The body's claims match the diff and the run below. "Once a render pass is through" means the App-worker pass that decided the rows, before its update is sent, which is the state `isEmbodied()` reads.

---

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: An edit survives losing its cell by default, because the draft lives in the App Worker. An editor whose state lives only in its DOM opts out per column and is cancelled loudly. And an IME composition is not such state: the composed text reaches the draft as it is typed.
